title: Reynolds-number effects and the energy-spectrum balance: how the ranges grow, and what the balance says about each
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b passed round 2 (0 blocking)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: The slide captions attribute the exponent data to Mydlarski and Warhaft (1998) and the kurtosis data to Van Atta and Antonia (1980); neither source was opened. The empirical curve p = 5/3 - 8 Re_lambda^(-3/4) (L42 f0028) is printed on the slide and was checked only against the plotted curve and the plotted points; its provenance is unknown.
The slide (L42 f0041) and the speech (L42 20:47) give 4 for the kurtosis of a Gaussian variable; the value is 3. The speech says 'indefinite decrease' where the slide and the plot say increase.

L42 about 940-955 s: the speech places the integral-scale Reynolds number at Re_lambda = 10^4 'more than a hundred thousand ... close to a million'; the book's relation (15.1) gives 1.5e7 (Re_L) and 6.7e6 (Re_0). The speech defers the exact value to an earlier relation.

The speech 'ten to fifteen percent of the energy is contained in the dissipation range' (L42 about 1052-1058 s) matches the energy above kappa_EI in the model (10.0 to 12.3 %), not the dissipation range alone; the lecture's own definition of the range there is not stated.
The lecture's reasons for T_kappa(0) = 0 and T_kappa(infinity) = 0 (no energy below, no scales above) are replaced by the conservation argument of chapter 12, (12.22).
ASR: 'tau EI' = T_EI; 'Tk' = T_kappa; 'Kolbogorov' = Kolmogorov; 'k eta u eta squared' = eta u_eta^2; 'RE lambda' = Re_lambda; the slide's production spectrum is not derived in the lectures.
The slide's source for the module (Module 08 Source slide) was not viewed in these two recordings; the chapter makes no source attribution for the module's figures beyond the slide captions.
The nominal factors 1/6 and 60 in ell_EI and ell_DI are the lecture's 'say' values with no stated justification (chapter 10); every number using them inherits that status.
